question: Where did Ahaz make altars?
explanation: He made him altars in every corner of Jerusalem.

question: Where did Ahaz make high places to burn incense to other gods?
choices: In every several city of Judah
explanation: In every several city of Judah he made high places to burn incense unto other gods.

question: Into what was Ahaz not brought after his burial in Jerusalem?
choices: The sepulchres of the kings of Israel
explanation: They buried him in the city, even in Jerusalem: but they brought him not into the sepulchres of the kings of Israel.

question: How far did Oded say the rage of Israel's slaughter reached?
explanation: Ye have slain them in a rage that reacheth up unto heaven.

question: What did Ahaz do in the time of his distress?
choices: Trespassed yet more against the LORD
explanation: In the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against the LORD: this is that king Ahaz.

question: What were the gods of Damascus to Ahaz and all Israel?
explanation: They were the ruin of him, and of all Israel.

question: Who had again come and smitten Judah and carried away captives?
explanation: For again the Edomites had come and smitten Judah, and carried away captives.

question: How old was Hezekiah when he began to reign?
explanation: Hezekiah began to reign when he was five and twenty years old.

question: What did Hezekiah first command concerning the house of the Lord?
explanation: He prioritized cleansing the neglected temple.

question: What reason did Hezekiah give for Judah's troubles?
choices: Their fathers had trespassed and forsaken the Lord
explanation: He traces Judah's trouble to covenant unfaithfulness.

question: On which day of the first month did they make an end of cleansing the house?
explanation: In the sixteenth day of the first month they made an end.

question: What happened when the burnt offering began at the restored service?
choices: The song of the Lord began also with the trumpets
explanation: Sacrifice and praise resumed together.

question: Who gathered the priests and Levites into the east street?
explanation: Hezekiah brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them into the east street.

question: What did Hezekiah do to the doors of the house of the LORD in the first month?
explanation: He opened the doors of the house of the LORD, and repaired them.

question: What was the name of Hezekiah's mother?
explanation: His mother's name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.

question: Which king had cast away the vessels of the temple in his transgression?
explanation: All the vessels which king Ahaz in his reign did cast away in his transgression were prepared and sanctified.

question: Into which brook did the Levites carry the uncleanness?
explanation: The Levites took the uncleanness to carry it out abroad into the brook Kidron.

question: Which instruments did the Levites stand with in the house of the LORD?
explanation: He set the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, with psalteries, and with harps.

question: Who helped the priests when there were too few to flay the burnt offerings?
explanation: The priests were too few, so their brethren the Levites did help them.

question: Why did Hezekiah and all the people rejoice at the end of the chapter?
explanation: Hezekiah rejoiced, and all the people, that God had prepared the people: for the thing was done suddenly.

question: Where did the priests go to cleanse the house of the LORD?
choices: The inner part of the house
explanation: The priests went into the inner part of the house of the LORD, to cleanse it.

question: What did the priests do with the blood of the killed animals?
explanation: The priests received the blood, and sprinkled it on the altar.

question: How many years did Hezekiah reign in Jerusalem?
explanation: He reigned nine and twenty years in Jerusalem.

question: In which month of his first year did Hezekiah open the temple doors?
explanation: He in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of the LORD.

question: What did Hezekiah tell the Levites to carry forth out of the holy place?
explanation: Sanctify the house of the LORD, and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place.

question: What had the fathers done to the lamps?
explanation: They shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps.

question: What had happened to the sons, daughters and wives of Judah, according to Hezekiah?
explanation: Our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity.

question: What did Hezekiah say was in his heart to make with the LORD?
explanation: It is in mine heart to make a covenant with the LORD God of Israel, that his fierce wrath may turn away from us.

question: What did Hezekiah say the LORD had chosen the Levites to do?
choices: Stand before him and serve him
explanation: The LORD hath chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and that ye should minister unto him, and burn incense.

question: Where did the priests bring the uncleanness before the Levites took it away?
choices: Into the court of the house of the LORD
Into the porch of the palace
explanation: They brought out all the uncleanness into the court of the house of the LORD, and the Levites took it.

question: Besides the altar of burnt offering, which table did they say they had cleansed?
explanation: We have cleansed the altar of burnt offering, and the shewbread table, with all the vessels thereof.

question: How many bullocks were brought for the sin offering?
explanation: They brought seven bullocks, and seven rams, and seven lambs, and seven he goats.

question: Besides the kingdom and Judah, what was the sin offering for?
explanation: A sin offering for the kingdom, and for the sanctuary, and for Judah.

question: What did the congregation do to the he goats before the king?
explanation: They brought forth the he goats before the king and the congregation; and they laid their hands upon them.

question: For whom did the king command the burnt offering and sin offering to be made?
explanation: The king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Israel.

question: Whose words did Hezekiah tell the Levites to sing praise with, along with Asaph's?
explanation: Hezekiah commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the LORD with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer.

question: Why could the priests not flay all the burnt offerings?
explanation: The priests were too few, so that they could not flay all the burnt offerings.

question: Whose daughter was Hezekiah's mother Abijah?
explanation: His mother's name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.

question: Mahath, one of the Levites who arose, was the son of whom?
explanation: Then the Levites arose, Mahath the son of Amasai.

question: Which two men are named as sons of Asaph among the Levites who arose?
explanation: Of the sons of Asaph; Zechariah, and Mattaniah.

question: To what did Hezekiah say the LORD had delivered Judah and Jerusalem?
explanation: He hath delivered them to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing, as ye see with your eyes.

question: Where did Hezekiah gather the priests and Levites together?
choices: Into the porch of the temple
Into the court of the palace
explanation: He brought in the priests and the Levites, and gathered them together into the east street.

question: On which day of the first month did they come to the porch of the LORD?
explanation: On the eighth day of the month came they to the porch of the LORD.

question: How many bullocks did the congregation bring as burnt offerings?
explanation: The number of the burnt offerings was threescore and ten bullocks, an hundred rams, and two hundred lambs.

question: How many lambs did the congregation bring as burnt offerings?
explanation: The burnt offerings were threescore and ten bullocks, an hundred rams, and two hundred lambs.

question: How many oxen were among the consecrated things?
explanation: The consecrated things were six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep.

question: Who is named with Nathan the prophet as one by whom David's commandment about the instruments came?
explanation: According to the commandment of David, and of Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet.

question: Who stood with the trumpets while the Levites stood with David's instruments?
explanation: The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

question: Who were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves, the priests or the Levites?
explanation: The Levites were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests.

question: What accompanied the fat of the peace offerings for every burnt offering?
explanation: The burnt offerings were in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings, and the drink offerings for every burnt offering.

question: What did Hezekiah invite the congregation to bring into the house of the LORD?
explanation: Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings into the house of the LORD.

question: What had the fathers turned away from the habitation of the LORD?
explanation: They have turned away their faces from the habitation of the LORD, and turned their backs.

question: To whom did Hezekiah send letters inviting them to keep Passover?
explanation: He invited both southern and northern remnants.

question: Why was the Passover kept in the second month instead of the first?
choices: The priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently and the people were not gathered
explanation: Practical and ceremonial reasons delayed it to the second month.

question: How did the people of Ephraim, Manasseh and Zebulun react to the king's messengers?
choices: They laughed them to scorn and mocked them
explanation: They mocked the messengers, though some humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.

question: What did Hezekiah do for the people who ate the passover without being cleansed?
choices: Prayed that the good Lord would pardon every one
explanation: Hezekiah interceded for the sincere though ceremonially unprepared worshipers.

question: How does the chapter describe the joy in Jerusalem at this Passover?
choices: There was great joy such as had not been since the days of Solomon
explanation: The feast was marked by remarkable joy and unity.

question: What did the people do after the great feast ended?
choices: Went out and destroyed images and high places
explanation: The people extended reform throughout the land.

question: What did Hezekiah appoint for the priests and Levites?
explanation: He arranged the ministers in ordered courses for worship.

question: What did the people bring in abundance once the commandment spread?
explanation: They responded generously with support for worship.

question: How did the priest Azariah explain the great heaps of provision?
choices: Since the people began to bring offerings, the Lord hath blessed his people
explanation: Azariah says the abundance came from God's blessing.

question: How does the chapter summarize Hezekiah's work?
choices: He wrought that which was good and right and truth before the Lord
explanation: Hezekiah is praised for faithful reform and administration.

question: Which Assyrian king came against Judah's fenced cities?
explanation: Sennacherib invaded Judah after Hezekiah's reforms.

question: How did Hezekiah prepare Jerusalem militarily?
choices: By stopping the waters and strengthening the walls
explanation: He took defensive steps and stopped the water sources.

question: What encouragement did Hezekiah give the people?
choices: With us is the Lord our God to help us and fight our battles
explanation: Hezekiah urged them to trust the Lord rather than fear Assyria.

question: Which prophet joined Hezekiah in crying to heaven about Sennacherib's threats?
explanation: Isaiah and Hezekiah prayed together.

question: How did God save Jerusalem from Assyria?
choices: By sending an angel who cut off the mighty men
explanation: The Lord sent an angel who destroyed the Assyrian forces.

question: What did Manasseh rebuild that Hezekiah had broken down?
explanation: Manasseh restored idolatrous worship sites.

question: What shocking practice did Manasseh engage in regarding his children?
choices: He caused his children to pass through the fire
explanation: Manasseh committed abominations including child sacrifice.

question: What happened after the Lord brought the captains of Assyria against Manasseh?
choices: He was bound with fetters and carried to Babylon
explanation: Manasseh was bound with fetters and carried to Babylon.

question: How did Manasseh respond in his affliction?
choices: He humbled himself greatly and prayed
explanation: His affliction led to real humility and prayer.

question: What contrast is made with Amon, who followed Manasseh?
choices: Amon humbled not himself and trespassed more and more
explanation: Amon did not learn from his father's repentance.

question: How old was Josiah when he began to reign?
explanation: Josiah was eight years old when he became king.

question: What did Josiah begin to do in the eighth year of his reign while yet young?
choices: Seek the God of David his father
explanation: Josiah began seeking the Lord early in life.

question: What book was found in the house of the Lord during repairs?
choices: The book of the law of the Lord by Moses
explanation: Hilkiah found the law in the temple.

question: How did Josiah react when he heard the words of the law?
explanation: He tore his clothes in grief and fear.

question: What message did Huldah give specifically to Josiah because his heart was tender?
choices: He would be gathered to his grave in peace
explanation: Judgment would come on Judah, but not in Josiah's lifetime.

question: What major feast did Josiah keep unto the Lord in Jerusalem?
explanation: Josiah kept a remarkable Passover.

question: How does the chapter describe this Passover in comparison with earlier times?
choices: There was no passover like that kept in Israel from Samuel's days
explanation: It was unparalleled since the days of Samuel.

question: Which Egyptian ruler did Josiah go out against at Megiddo?
explanation: Josiah confronted Pharaoh-necho at Megiddo.

question: What warning did Pharaoh-necho send to Josiah?
choices: That he came only against another house and God had commanded him to make haste
That Egypt would worship in Jerusalem
explanation: Necho warned Josiah not to oppose what God had permitted.

question: What happened to Josiah in the battle?
choices: Archers shot him and he died
explanation: Josiah was wounded by archers and died.

question: Who was made king by the people after Josiah's death?
explanation: Jehoahaz was first made king after Josiah.

question: What pattern marked the remaining kings of Judah in this chapter?
choices: They rebuilt the high places of the Lord
They did evil in the sight of the Lord
explanation: The final kings are repeatedly described as doing evil.

question: Why did God send messengers to his people again and again before the fall?
choices: He had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place
explanation: The Lord persistently warned them out of compassion.

question: What happened to the house of God under Nebuchadnezzar's invasion?
choices: It was burned, and Jerusalem's walls were broken down
explanation: Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed by Babylon.

question: Which Persian king issued the decree that the Lord had charged him to build a house in Jerusalem?
explanation: The book ends with Cyrus's decree of return and rebuilding.
